# Actors Reference

Complete reference for reading actors — people and agents — from Glassfrog:
the `glassfrog actors` directory and single read, and the `glassfrog assignments`
list.

## Overview

An actor is a person (`per_…`) or an AI agent (`agt_…`) in the organization. The
Actor Reads slice is a find-then-read surface, plus a standalone assignments list:

| Command | API operation | Purpose |
|---|---|---|
| `actors` | `GET /actors` | List/find actors (discovery) |
| `actors <id>` | `GET /actors/{id}` | Read one actor and their governance footprint |
| `assignments <actor-id>` | `GET /actors/{actor_id}/assignments` | List the roles an actor fills |

`actors` (no positional) is the directory list; `actors <id>` (one positional) is
the single read — the same command, branching on the positional. None of these
reads is feature-gated: agents are reachable through `/actors` without the
`ai_integration` flag. These are read-only — actor administration (invite, update,
delete, assign/un-assign) is deliberately out of scope.

Codebase enrichment skipped — not attempted. This reference is based on the
interface contracts only.

## `glassfrog actors` — list and find actors

### Synopsis

```
glassfrog actors [--kind KIND] [--role-id ROLE_ID] [--query TEXT|-q TEXT]
                 [--first-page] [--per-page N] [--base-url URL] [-o FORMAT]
```

Takes **no positional argument** — any positional is a usage error. Walks every
page to completion by default. Filters combine; with none, every actor in the
organization is requested.

| Flag | Short | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `--kind` | — | string | — | Filter by actor type, sent as `kind`. Validated locally against `human`/`agent`; an unsupported value is a usage error with no API call. |
| `--role-id` | — | string | — | Filter to the actors filling a role (`role_…`), sent as `role_id`. Passed through unvalidated; a malformed value returns `400`. |
| `--query` | `-q` | string | — | Free-text search over actor names, sent as `q`. Passed through unvalidated; `--query ""` behaves as no filter. |
| `--first-page` | — | bool | false | Fetch only the first page; signal on stderr if more exist. |
| `--per-page` | — | int | API max (500) | Page size for the walk. |

Each row carries the actor's `per_`/`agt_` id, a `kind` badge, and name — enough to
tell a person from an agent and carry the id into the single read. An empty result
exits successfully.

### Supported `--kind` values

`human`, `agent`.

## `glassfrog actors <id>` — read one actor with their footprint

### Synopsis

```
glassfrog actors <id> [--include LIST] [--base-url URL] [-o FORMAT]
```

| Argument | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `<id>` | string | yes (for the single read) | The actor's id — `per_…` (human) or `agt_…` (agent). The same command reads either kind. Passed through unvalidated; an unknown id returns `404`. Exactly one positional; a second is a usage error. |

| Flag | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `--include` | string (comma-separated) | — | Embed related resources inline, sent as `include`. Validated locally against `roles`/`assignments`; an unsupported value is a usage error with no API call. Multiple values combine (`--include roles,assignments`). |

### Supported `--include` values

| Value | Embeds |
|---|---|
| `roles` | The actor's governance footprint — each role's name, purpose, accountabilities, and domains. |
| `assignments` | The actor↔role assignments inline on the actor. |

With no `--include`, the bare actor is read — id, name, kind, timestamps. The
single read is unpaginated (any embedded arrays arrive inline in the one response).
Embedded sections render explicit-absence markers (`(no purpose set)`, `(none)`)
rather than blanks, and never appear unless requested.

### Mode separation

The directory filter flags are list-only; `--include` is single-only:

| Invocation | Result |
|---|---|
| `actors` (0 args, optional filters) | Directory list |
| `actors <id>` (+ optional `--include`) | Single read |
| `actors <id> --kind …`/`--role-id …`/`--query …`/`--first-page` | Usage error (2), no request — filters are list-only |
| `actors --include …` (no id) | Usage error (2), no request — `--include` is single-only |
| `actors <id> <id2>` | Usage error (2), no request — at most one positional |

## `glassfrog assignments <actor-id>` — list the roles an actor fills

### Synopsis

```
glassfrog assignments <actor-id> [--first-page] [--per-page N] [--base-url URL] [-o FORMAT]
```

| Argument | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `<actor-id>` | string | yes | The actor whose assignments to read (`per_…` or `agt_…`). Passed through unvalidated; an unknown id returns `404`. Exactly one required. |

**Filter flags**: none. The endpoint accepts no query filter beyond pagination, and
its default `include=role` already embeds each filled role's
`{id, type, name, purpose, parent_role_id}` — so no `--include` flag is offered.

| Flag | Short | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `--first-page` | — | bool | false | Fetch only the first page; signal on stderr if more exist. |
| `--per-page` | — | int | API max (500) | Page size for the walk. |

Walks every page to completion by default. Each row leads with the filled role
(`role_` id, name, purpose, parent role) and adds the assignment's `focus` and
`elected_until`. Nullable fields (`focus`, `elected_until`, `purpose`, parent role)
render explicit-absence markers (`(none)`, `(not an elected seat)`,
`(top-level)`) rather than blanks. An actor that fills no roles produces an empty
list and exits successfully.

> `assignments <actor-id>` reads the filling relationship from the *actor* end.
> The same `Assignment` resource read from the *role* end — the actors who fill a
> role — is `glassfrog roles`' filler read (Role Fillers). The two are deliberately
> separate directions of one resource.

## Completeness

The paginated commands (`actors` list, `assignments`) never silently truncate:

- **Default** — walk every page and render the complete set.
- **`--first-page`** — one page; if more exist, a "more exist" note on stderr, exit
  `0`.
- **Mid-walk failure** — the rows gathered so far, flagged incomplete with the cause
  on stderr, exit non-zero.

The single `actors <id>` read is unpaginated, with no completeness signalling.

## Inherited flags

| Flag | Owner | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `--base-url` | 011 | Override the API base URL. |
| `-o`, `--output` | 020/035 | `full` (default) \| `compact` \| `json` \| `yaml` \| a user-template ref. |

Successful output is rendered by Output Format Selection in the resolved format;
`json`/`yaml` emit the structured document verbatim, `full`/`compact` render the
human projection. No command defines its own format flag.

## Error reference

Failure rendering is format-aware: `json`/`yaml` write the unified error envelope
to stdout; `full`/`compact` write the diagnostic (cause + next step) to stderr.
Every diagnostic names the cause and a next step and never includes the token. No
actor command introduces its own exit code.

| Condition | Outcome | Exit |
|---|---|---|
| Success (incl. empty list) | Success | 0 |
| Positional on `actors` list, list filter with an id, `--include` with no id, two positionals, unsupported `--kind`/`--include`, missing `assignments` id, unknown flag, invalid `--output`, base-URL config error, no usable token | UsageError | 2 |
| Unreadable/malformed credential file | RuntimeError | 1 |
| Unknown id (`404`), malformed `--role-id` (`400`), other `4xx`/`5xx`, response shape mismatch | APIError | 3 |
| Permission (`401`/`403`) | PermissionError | 4 |
| Rate limited (`429`) | RateLimited | 5 |
| Could not reach the wire | NetworkUnavailable | 6 |
